text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
An increase in electricity rates by 9.92 percent may accelerate inflation and lift monthly inflation rates to one percent.
-- 15 CONSORTIA ENTER BATTLE FOR CELULAR LINES
Fifteen consortia have entered bids to operate B Band cellular services.

Banco Safra and a group of 12 Japanese trading and steel companies led by Nippon Steel have joined Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim in a consortium to bid at the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD.
President Cardoso said the globalized economy created people that were 'unemployable' in the sense that they lost their place in the labor market due to technological advances.

Statements by top officials from Brazilian bank Bradesco have divided the opinion of a parliamentary committee probing a multimillion fraud involving state and municipal bonds as to whether large banks participated in the scam.
-- ROGUE RIO POLICE ARE ARRESTED AND EXPULSED
Another amateur video aired on national television showing Rio de Janeiro police officers beating and intimidating civilians has led to the arrest of six policemen allegedly involved in the incident.
Drug traffickers have been sabotaging roadworks near their Rio de Janeiro shantytown stronghold by stealing trucks from the construction company and forcing laborers to stop work by 4 p.m.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy. ((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151
